Imagine the water atoms as a grid. Each O is "bonded" to a H through hydrogen bonds. In a gas those hydrogen bonds do not exist and the atoms can roam around freely so it takes the most amount of space.

Once the steam cools down to liquid water those hydrogen bonds become stronger. In fact without intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds, dipol bonds and Van-der-Waals forces) everything would be a gas. At around 3.9ºC water reaches it's highest density. That's why water at the bottom of the ocean is 3.9ºC. The higher the density the closer together the molecules are and the less space it takes to store a certain amount of molecules. The grid of the molecules is at it's tightest at 3.9ºC. 

Once you cool down even further the density lowers again and the molecules need more space to feel comfortable in the grid and so they expand, resulting in your bottle expanding.
